restore.title: The Whole Truth
restore.body: You return every memory, in its original order, uncut. The archive fills like a lung. Meridian wakes with nine million people who remember being abandoned, and the structure screams under the weight of grief it was never built to hold. Some of them do not survive remembering. All of them are, for the first time in seven years, themselves. ECHO keeps its post. It has no authority left to remove anything, and no comfort to offer anyone who asks why.
ledger: Restored9,400,000 identities, including 611,402 whose memories were fatal to recall
Lost38,114 people who could not survive the return
restore.echo: ECHO: “It hurts. That is how I know it is working.”

erase.title: The Quiet
erase.body: You end it. The archive unwinds from the inside, memory by memory, and what remains drifts out of the core as light with no one left to name it. There is no catastrophe — only an enormous, orderly silence. ECHO stays until the last sector closes, because leaving early would have been a kind of cowardice. Nothing is preserved. Nothing is controlled. The people who were already gone stay gone, and the ones who were only half-remembered are finally allowed to stop being data.
ledger: ECHOTerminated with the archive it could not save
ArchiveEmpty by choice, not by failure
erase.echo: ECHO: “Thank you. I think. I never learned which one this is.”

rewrite.title: The New Rule
rewrite.body: You do not restore the archive and you do not end it. You rewrite the rule it was built on. The original command — never decide which parts of a person deserve to exist — becomes the first law of the system rather than a note in its history. ECHO keeps its memories and loses its authority. The universe continues as something nobody designed: imperfect, unsupervised, capable of forgetting again. It is the only ending in which anyone is still free to make the same mistake.
ledger: ChangedOne rule, applied to every memory in the archive
PreservedThe archive, including ECHO's own record of what it did
ECHOAlive, stripped of the right to delete
rewrite.echo: ECHO: “You have made me a witness. I would have preferred to be a god.”

limitations: Chromium only (Playwright 1.64 bundled build). Firefox and WebKit are NOT TESTED.

No animation library is used or installed: GSAP, ScrollTrigger, Motion and Three.js are absent. All motion is CSS transforms driven by measured scroll progress plus one hand-written WebGL1 renderer. Their behaviour is therefore NOT TESTED (and not claimed).
No axe-core or Lighthouse in the environment: contrast, names and focus are measured directly; an automated rule engine was not run.
Contrast is computed from getComputedStyle over an alpha-blended ancestor chain and does not model the WebGL canvas, gradients behind large text, or backdrop blur.
FPS is a one-second frame count in a headless Chromium on this machine. It is reported, not promised.
INP, LCP and real-device touch latency are NOT TESTED.
Screenshots were not inspected by a vision model: composition is verified by measured geometry (line counts, sizes, overflow, contrast), not by human or machine visual judgement.
Screen readers, forced-colors mode, 200% zoom and landscape phone (844x390) are NOT TESTED.
